body.statement:
Suppose that the constructed law \(P^{\star}\) obeys the displayed fourth-moment envelope, that is,
\[
 \max_{1\le g\le3}\max_{1\le t\le3}
 E_{P_O^{\star}}[|Y_t|^4\mid G=g]\le M_4.
\]
Then the corrected PT vector is \(q_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=(0,0)^{\prime}\), its profiled normal \(R_{\mathrm{PT}}\) has rank one, and \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_I\). The uniquely identified SC weights are \((1/2,1/2)\), while minimizing the PT Gram criterion over donor weights summing to one gives inverse-change-variance weights \((4/5,1/5)\). The exact efficiency bounds are
\[
 V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=\frac{42}{5},\qquad
 V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})=\frac{1625}{184},\qquad
 V_U(P^{\star})=\frac{39}{4},
\]
and hence
\[
 V_U(P^{\star})-V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=\frac{27}{20},\qquad
 V_U(P^{\star})-V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})=\frac{169}{184}.
\]
The union QP fixes the final donor coefficients at \((1/2,1/2)\); its required SC preperiod-normal coefficient differs from the SC oracle coefficient, so both one-sided Gram discrepancies are strictly positive. The same strict inequalities hold on a relatively open region preserving the fourth-moment envelope, full rank, unequal positive donor-change variances, and unequal SC and PT-oracle weights.
body.justification: With one stratum, the corrected composition gradient is zero, so the exact strict gaps continue to certify that the frontier has empirical content.
body.gap: The branchwise papers do not exhibit a legal intersection region with distinct canonical gradients and a strict union-regularity cost.
body.consumer: The witness is a calibration design for checking the finite lower-bound quadratic program; this paper certifies no accompanying standard-error software.
body.proof_tex:
There is one stratum and every group has probability \(1/3\). Thus the support and overlap margins hold because \(p_X=1\) and \(1/3>\epsilon_0\). No anticipation holds by construction. Every untreated final mean change is zero, so conditional parallel trends holds and
\[
 D=(0,0)^{\prime},\qquad \delta_1^0=0,\qquad q_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=(0,0)^{\prime}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The augmented donor matrix and target vector are
\[
 B=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\-1&1\\-2&2\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad a=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad B^{\prime}B=\begin{pmatrix}6&-4\\-4&6\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The eigenvalues are \(2\) and \(10\), so the SC rank margin holds since \(\kappa_0<1\). Solving \(Bw=a\) gives the unique weights \(w=(1/2,1/2)^{\prime}\), which also reproduce the period-three untreated mean. The assumed fourth-moment inequality supplies the remaining model condition. Hence \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_I\). Since \(K=1\), each branch contrast equals its own treated average, so
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\chi_{\mathrm{SC}}=\chi_0=0.
 \tag{3}
\]
Thus the corrected composition term changes none of the following variance calculations.

Define \(z_{g,t}=3\mathbf 1\{G=g\}\varepsilon_{g,t}\). Direct differentiation of a conditional cell mean shows that \(z_{g,t}\) is its mean-zero influence variable. The variables are pairwise orthogonal, with variances by time within group
\[
 (3,3,3),\qquad (3,3/2,3/2),\qquad (6,6,6).
 \tag{4}
\]
The PT face, parameterized by the donor-two weight \(v\), is
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{PT}}(v)=(z_{1,3}-z_{1,2})
 -v(z_{2,3}-z_{2,2})-(1-v)(z_{3,3}-z_{3,2}).
 \tag{5}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \|\psi_{\mathrm{PT}}(v)\|_0^2=6+3v^2+12(1-v)^2.
 \tag{6}
\]
The derivative is \(30v-24\), so the unique minimizer is \(v=4/5\), and
\[
 V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=6+3(4/5)^2+12(1/5)^2=\frac{42}{5}.
 \tag{7}
\]
For \(J=2\), the donor-change contrast has positive variance \(15\); hence the PT normal Gram has rank one.

For SC, \(u=(0,-2,1)^{\prime}\) spans \(\ker(B^{\prime})\). Differentiating the full-rank normal equations yields
\[
 \dot w=(B^{\prime}B)^{-1}B^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B,w).
 \tag{8}
\]
The unrestricted SC cell-mean coefficients, ordered by time within groups one, two, and three, are
\[
 (-2/5,-4/5,1),\qquad (1/5,2/5,-1/2),\qquad (1/5,2/5,-1/2).
 \tag{9}
\]
Adding \(\beta u^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B,w)\) changes only preperiod coefficients. Using (4), their variance contribution is
\[
 Q(\beta)=\frac{207}{8}\beta^2+\frac35\beta+\frac{99}{25}.
 \tag{10}
\]
It is uniquely minimized at \(\beta^{\mathrm{or}}=-4/345\), with minimum \(91/23\). The final-period contribution is \(39/8\), and therefore
\[
 V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})=\frac{39}{8}+\frac{91}{23}=\frac{1625}{184}.
 \tag{11}
\]

SC normals have only preperiod coordinates, so equality with the PT face forces \(v=1/2\) from the final donor coefficients. Equality of the preperiod coefficients then forces \(\beta=-1/5\), giving the unique common representative with coefficients
\[
 (0,-1,1),\qquad (0,1/2,-1/2),\qquad (0,1/2,-1/2).
 \tag{12}
\]
Its variance is
\[
 V_U(P^{\star})=6+3(1/2)^2+12(1/2)^2=\frac{39}{4}.
 \tag{13}
\]
The PT oracle has \(v=4/5\ne1/2\), and the SC oracle has \(\beta=-4/345\ne-1/5\). The one-sided criteria in \(\mathrm{thm{:}oracle\text{-}adaptation\text{-}frontier}\) therefore make both discrepancies strictly positive. Subtraction gives
\[
 V_U-V_{\mathrm{PT}}=\frac{27}{20},
 \qquad V_U-V_{\mathrm{SC}}=\frac{169}{184}.
 \tag{14}
\]
All finite-support Gram entries, unique quadratic minimizers, and minimized values vary continuously with cell probabilities, means, and second moments while the nonzero spectral margins persist. At \(P^{\star}\), full rank, positive unequal change variances, unequal oracle weights, and both strict gaps hold. Hence they persist on a relatively open intersection neighborhood satisfying the fourth-moment envelope. This proves the final stability assertion without moving any weight or moment boundary.
